analysis.title: Record Tech Selling, Extreme Shorts... What Could Possibly Go Wrong
key_insights: NDX remains in the same range it has held since May despite AI crash narratives. Chasing momentum at either range extreme has continued to lose money.

GS PB data show global technology stocks had the largest two-week net selling on record (10+ years of data) between October 5 and 16, 3.3 standard deviations below normal. The selling came from both long liquidations and fresh shorting.

GS PB data show short sales outpacing long buying 5:1 month-to-date, which pushed short leverage close to five-year highs. NDX has not broken its range, which the note calls potential fuel for an upside squeeze.
GS derivatives desk suggests buying QQQ Nov 6, 2026 740/760 call spreads for $4.60 (spot $722.50) as a defined-risk way to keep upside exposure into mega-cap tech earnings, the FOMC and US midterms.

sector_views.rationale: Record net selling and near-record short leverage in global tech set up a possible short squeeze, but NDX is still inside its range since May.

earnings_insights: Mega-cap tech earnings are listed as part of the packed catalyst calendar that could trigger a sharp move higher. No figures are given.
